content:
Carla S: Heads-up — multiple customers (incl. Raj K) reporting repeated 503s and short request timeouts from hosted inference since ~02:10 UTC. Support ticket #3241 escalated. Attaching repro and recent logs. Can we stand a quick war room?
Ben C: Oncall — joining. Any deploys around that time? link to runbook: https://intranet/runbooks/hosted-5xx ? I'll pull ingress + gateway metrics.
Diego R: Not seeing recent deploys. Ingress spike looks client-side fanout + backend KV thrash. Quick log samples:
```
[error] 2026-03-18T02:12:13Z host-gw: upstream_response=503 route=/v1/generate reason="kv-cache-miss/stall"
[warn] 2026-03-18T02:12:15Z batcher: queue_len=420 busy_workers=16 latency_p90=1500ms
[info] 2026-03-18T02:12:16Z auth-proxy: backend=keydb timeout=1200ms
```
Carla S: Repro we got from Raj (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"r-instruct-3b","input":"hi"}' -v
# returns intermittent 503s, p50 returns ~800ms then 503s in bursts
```
Diego R: Pattern: lots of small concurrent requests (short seq-len) so batching overhead + KV cache misses amplify latency; KV backend shows eviction storms. Also seeing auth-proxy 504s coincidentally.
Alice M: I'm enabling the circuit breaker to short-circuit heavy flows to reduce fanout and will bump autoscaler temporarily. Also plan to purge cache warm-up keys and adjust batcher throttle. Applying now.
Alice M: Command I'm running to purge warmup keys: `kubectl exec kv-warmup -- /app/purge_warmup --prefix=warmup-`
deploy-bot: Autoscaler: replica_count increased 4 -> 8 for pool hosted-inference-prod (triggered by alice-m). Canary rollback: initiated.
Ben C: Can we route big customers to a dedicated fallback pool while we stabilize? Erin, can you prepare a short customer status and coordinate with support? Raj K: from customer side — pattern started 02:09 UTC, bursts every 2-3 minutes, short requests mostly. Your curl reproducer matches our traffic.
Diego R: After purge and scale I'm seeing 503 rate down ~60%, p50 latency for short requests down from ~900ms -> ~210ms. Still watching KV eviction counters. Long-term fixes: change eviction policy to avoid cascade, prewarm on deploy, better backpressure in batcher.
Alice M: Also rolling a quick patch to batcher to apply a 20ms micro-throttle for tiny requests to avoid queue explosion. Patch pushed to prod canary.
Carla S: Action items: Diego = root cause writeup (kv eviction + small-request fanout), Alice = mitigation runbook + ops playbook updates, Ben = runbook tests & automation (auto-rollback on kv-miss spike), Erin = customer comms + status page, I'll own postmortem doc and timeline. All owners please add links and logs to the doc.
Ben C: I'll add a new checklist item: "thundering-small-reqs" with automated alerts on queue_len>300 + kv_miss_rate>5% and auto-scale.
deploy-bot: Canary: rollback complete. Autoscaler: scaled to 8. Patch 'batcher-micro-throttle' rolled out to 30% -> 100%.
Erin P: Drafting status update for affected customers: brief apology, impact window, mitigations performed, ETA for full postmortem. Sharing in #customer-comms for review.
Raj K: Appreciate the fast response. We'll standby for the postmortem and confirm if routing to a dedicated pool is needed for our traffic pattern.
Carla S: War room closing for now — immediate mitigation successful, monitoring in watch mode. Postmortem doc assigned to me, meeting scheduled tomorrow 10:00 UTC to review timeline, root cause, and permanent mitigations. Postmortem link (placeholder): https://intranet/postmortems/3304509876-thundering-gateway-503s. If this reoccurs, ping #incidents with "reopen". :eyes:
Ben C: :thumbsup: will update runbook and add automated rollback + playbook tests.
Diego R: I'll follow up with metrics dashboard changes (kv-miss, batcher-queue) and an alert runbook.
Alice M: Filed PRs for eviction-policy change and prewarm hook. Will shepherd through review today.
Erin P: Customer comms sent to affected list; support ticket #3241 updated.
Carla S: Thanks team — good work. Closing thread.
